headline: US charges 3 men over alleged Iran-backed terror plots incl. RAF Fairford
dek: [VERIFIED FACT -- the indictment] The US DOJ unsealed an 8-count superseding indictment on Tue Nov 10 charging Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi (dual Iranian-Iraqi, 32, in US custody since May), Mohsen Mohajeri (Iranian, 48) and Mohammad Ali al-Hassani (Iraqi, 35) with terrorism-related…
sources: US Department of Justice / US Attorney's Office SDNY (8-count superseding indictment, Manhattan federal court); Manhattan US Attorney Jamie McDonald; Attorney General Todd Blanche; FBI Director Kash Patel
fault_line: Terror plot or government cover-up: were the Fairford vans an Iranian terror cell, or fuel thieves — and did the UK government downplay a terror threat on a US bomber base?

sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- the indictment] The US DOJ unsealed an 8-count superseding indictment on Tue Nov 10 charging Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi (dual Iranian-Iraqi, 32, in US custody since May), Mohsen Mohajeri (Iranian, 48) and Mohammad Ali al-Hassani (Iraqi, 35) with terrorism-related offences, incl. conspiracy to provide material support to Kataib Hezbollah and the IRGC and conspiracy to bomb a place of public use. [VERIFIED FACT -- the Fairford plot] Prosecutors allege al-Hassani orchestrated a Sept 2026 plot against RAF Fairford, Gloucestershire, a British base housing US B-1 bombers used in the war on Iran: associates procured 3 vans, barrels of fuel, researched chemical accelerants and bought metal objects as shrapnel; on Sept 26-27 the vans approached the base and British police stopped them at a roadblock after a local resident reported suspicious activity. The US later withdrew B-1 bombers from Fairford on force-protection grounds. [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- the prison-cell direction] Prosecutors allege al-Saadi, held in solitary confinement at the Metropolitan Detention Centre, Brooklyn, used coded messages in phone/video calls to his mother and sister in Iraq to direct the plot and give final approval. [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- the campaign] The indictment links the defendants to nearly 20 alleged terrorist attacks/attempted attacks across Europe and the US, incl. arson, explosives attacks and a near-fatal stabbing targeting Jewish communities, many claimed under the name Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamiya (HAYI). [VERIFIED FACT -- UK side] UK police charged 2 men (Mohmed Ahmad Abdulkarim, Nouman Essghir, both 24) under the National Security Act 2023 over the Fairford incident; 6 others arrested remain on police bail. NOTE: the Sept 27 Fairford vans incident itself was already in the record (Bessent-item context); the NEW development is the unsealed indictment naming the 3 men, the prison-cell direction allegation and the ~20-attack campaign.
sections.what_verified: 5 distinct publisher families with declared tiers: US DOJ/SDNY indictment (T1, primary source); The National (T2); Al Jazeera (T2, STATE QA); TRT World (T3, STATE TR); South China Morning Post (T3). NY Post, The Sun, Telegraph India and Uninvited Press also carry the story but have NO declared tier in the registry and do NOT count toward corroboration. PASS gate met (>=2 families).
sections.what_disputed: Iran has strongly denied any involvement in the Fairford incident. The charges are allegations that must be proven in court; al-Saadi pleaded not guilty to earlier charges. The 2 UK men charged under the National Security Act were allegedly directed by an Iranian man known only as 'Ali', identity unconfirmed. British police initially released 6 arrested men on bail. No evidence has been made public tying the ~20-attack campaign to a specific Iranian state order beyond the prosecutors' network allegation (IRGC + Kataib Hezbollah).
sections.why_matters: He was already locked in a Brooklyn prison cell — and prosecutors say he still ran a terror plot against US bombers in Britain. Iran's war has reached a British airbase, and the indictment names ~20 attacks.
